crawl_url.title: Crawl a URL
crawl_url.description: Fetch a page through Crawlbase's proxy network and return its body. The core of the product: it rotates IPs, handles blocks and, with a JavaScript token, renders the page in a real browser first. Only successful responses are billed, so retrying a failure costs nothing.

format.description: Response envelope. `json` wraps the body with metadata, `html` returns it raw, `md` converts to Markdown.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code to route the request through.

user_agent.description: A specific user agent to send instead of Crawlbase's own.

page_wait.description: Milliseconds to wait after load before capturing. JavaScript token only.

ajax_wait.description: Wait for network activity to settle before capturing. JavaScript token only.

scroll.description: Scroll the page to trigger lazy loading. JavaScript token only.

scroll_interval.description: How many seconds to keep scrolling for. JavaScript token only.

css_click_selector.description: A CSS selector to click before capturing. JavaScript token only.

screenshot.description: Capture a JPEG screenshot instead of the page body. JavaScript token only.

pdf.description: Render the page to PDF. JavaScript token only.

store.description: Keep the response in Crawlbase Storage so it can be fetched again without re-crawling.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request.

get_headers.description: Return the origin's response headers alongside the body.

get_cookies.description: Return the cookies the origin set.

output.description: The fetched page, in whatever format `format` asked for -- raw HTML, a JSON envelope, Markdown, a screenshot or a PDF.

crawl_url_async.title: Crawl a URL asynchronously
crawl_url_async.description: Queue a crawl and get a request id back immediately instead of waiting for the page. The result is delivered to `callback_url` or kept in Storage. The right shape for a large batch, where holding thousands of connections open is not viable.

async.description: Queue the request rather than waiting. Leave this true -- it is what makes the call asynchronous.

callback.description: Deliver the result to a callback url rather than only storing it.

callback_url.description: Where Crawlbase should POST the finished crawl.

callback_headers.description: Extra headers to send with the callback, as a header string.

format.description: Response envelope for the delivered result.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code to route through.

page_wait.description: Milliseconds to wait after load. JavaScript token only.

ajax_wait.description: Wait for network activity to settle. JavaScript token only.

output.description: A request id (`rid`) to correlate the later callback or Storage read with.

scrape_url.title: Scrape a URL into structured data
scrape_url.description: Fetch a page and return it as structured JSON rather than markup, using Crawlbase's per-site scrapers. `scraper` names which one to apply -- e.g. an Amazon product or a LinkedIn profile -- and the fields you get back depend on that choice.

scraper.description: Which per-site scraper to apply, e.g. "amazon-product-details".

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code to route through.

autoparse.description: Let Crawlbase pick the scraper from the url instead of naming one.

output.description: The page parsed into structured JSON by the chosen scraper.

find_leads.title: Find leads for a domain
find_leads.description: Look up the email addresses Crawlbase holds for a company domain, with names and roles where it has them. A different product from crawling -- it queries Crawlbase's own dataset rather than fetching a page.

domain.description: The company domain to look up, e.g. "example.com".

output.description: The leads found for that domain, each with an email address and whatever name and role data Crawlbase holds.

get_stored_page.title: Get a stored page
get_stored_page.description: Fetch a page Crawlbase kept in Storage, by its request id or by the original url. Reading from Storage does not re-crawl and is not billed as a crawl, which is what makes `store=true` on the crawl worthwhile.

rid.description: The request id of the stored page.

url.description: The original url, as an alternative to the request id.

output.description: The stored page in the requested format, with its original crawl metadata.

list_stored_rids.title: List stored request IDs
list_stored_rids.description: The request ids currently held in Storage, for reconciling what was crawled against what a downstream system has processed. Up to 10,000 per call, with a scroll cursor for more.

limit.description: How many request ids to return, up to 10,000.

scroll.description: Enable cursor paging rather than a single page.

scroll_id.description: Continue a previous scroll from this cursor.

scroll_order.description: Order to scroll the ids in.

output.description: A page of matching records, with whatever cursor or paging fields the provider returns.

get_storage_total_count.title: Count the stored pages
get_storage_total_count.description: How many pages Storage currently holds. Cheap enough to poll, and the quickest check that a bulk crawl actually landed.

get_stored_pages_bulk.title: Get stored pages in bulk
get_stored_pages_bulk.description: Fetch up to 100 stored pages in one call rather than one request each. `auto_delete` removes them as they are read, which is the usual pattern for draining a queue exactly once.

rids.description: The request ids to fetch, up to 100.

auto_delete.description: Delete each entry as it is returned, so it is not processed twice.

output.description: The stored pages for those request ids.

delete_stored_page.title: Delete a stored page
delete_stored_page.description: Remove one page from Storage by its request id. Irreversible -- re-obtaining the content means crawling the url again, which is billed.

rid.description: The request id of the entry to delete.

output.description: Confirmation that the record was deleted.

delete_stored_pages_bulk.title: Delete stored pages in bulk
delete_stored_pages_bulk.description: Remove many entries from Storage in one call. Irreversible, and it is easy to pass more ids than intended -- re-obtaining any of them means paying to crawl again.

output.description: The provider's response to the call.
